newsitem.title: USA: Fire aboard Cunard cruise liner, one dead.
newsitem.headline: Fire aboard Cunard cruise liner, one dead.

text.p: Fire broke out in a linen locker aboard a cruise ship near the Bahamas on Sunday, forcing hundreds of passengers to prepare to abandon ship as crew members fought the blaze, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
Cunard Line Ltd, owner of the 627-foot (190-metre) Cunard liner Vista Fjord, said a German crewman in his twenties died. It was not certain how he died, Cunard spokesman Bill Spears said.
The fire was extinguished after the ship, carrying 991 passengers and crew, pulled into port at Freeport, Bahamas, more than three hours after the crew radioed for help, a Coast Guard spokesman said.

The vessel put out a distress call from about 20 miles (32 km) south of Freeport, Bahamas, at 1:40 a.m. (0640 GMT), a few hours after its departure from Ft. Lauderdale on Saturday night enroute to Funchal on the Portuguese island of Madeira.

As its crew fought the fire and headed the ship toward Freeport, the Coast Guard dispatched a boat and a plane to help and three other cruise ships, the Veendam, Destiny and Leeward, diverted in case passengers had to abandon ship, Coast Guard Petty Officer David French said.
The Vista Fjord arrived at Freeport about 5:20 a.m. (0920 GMT) and the crew, with help from Bahamian firefighters, extinguished the blaze within an hour, French said.
"Any fire at sea looks serious. We were making the preparations as soon as we got the call," French said. "We asked the crew to brief the passengers, asking them to prepare to abandon ship."
Cunard Line said damage was contained to the linen locker area on the ship's third deck toward the stern, but could not confirm the fire was out.
"We need to get into the linen store itself, but we need to make sure it's cooled down," Spears said. "It is well under control. There is no further danger to passengers or crew."

Spears said the Vista Fjord would remain in Freeport for at least two days and then was "more likely than not" to continue the cruise on an altered schedule. Passengers would be able to stay on board, he said.
"The majority are staying on board and may continue with cruise," Spears said. "Some people may change their mind. One or two passengers have asked to return home."
The Coast Guard dispatched investigators to Freeport to look into the cause of the fire.
"We know where it started ... but our investigators will have to go over to figure out why it started," French said.
